answer: Each epoch the registry lists a finite set of places, and a keeper at each opens one jar of nectar, draws a phrase from a slip and speaks it once. A head must stand there, in its body, and give the keeper an echo: the phrase returned, then one original line on what it prevented. A thread from the keeper's spool binds the echo to the jar, and nectar pours only when the echo answers. Nothing can be pre-baked: the phrase exists only as the jar opens, and each keeper's thread is spent on use. A farm's tenth head needs a tenth place, a tenth keeper and a tenth body.
